alerts.header: Change at Table Mesa Station beginning Mon Mar 23.
alerts.description:
RTD will begin work March 23 to perform structural repairs at the Table Mesa Park-n-Ride. To ensure customer safety, the 18-month project will require temporary closure of the station plaza area and relocation of some bus gates.

Work to be completed includes improvements to the front stair tower on the north side of the parking structure, steel repairs to the awning that covers the plaza, and replacement of roofing, along with some structural concrete repairs in isolated locations within the parking garage. For the duration of the project, bus gates B and C in front of the parking garage will be temporarily closed.

    Customers arriving via the Flatiron Flyer (FF) or Airport (AB) routes will deboard at the bus stop located along Table Mesa Drive across from the Park-n-Ride.

    Eastbound customers departing on FF or AB routes will board at the south ramp boarding plaza on the south side of U.S. 36. Customers can take an elevator to Level 4 of the Park-n-Ride garage to access the pedestrian bridge over US 36 to the south ramp boarding plaza. Westbound customers will board at Gate E along Table Mesa Drive  

The project is estimated to be completed in September 2027. Details and project updates are available on RTD’s
website.

alerts.header: Change at Orchard Station beginning Thu Mar 26 due to construction.
alerts.description:
RTD is coordinating with local partners Goldsmith Metropolitan District and the City of Greenwood Village to ensure customer access to light rail during a six-month project to redevelop the green space at Orchard Station Park beginning March 26. Light rail service will not be affected by the project.

During the initial phase of work, which includes construction of a sound wall along I-25, crews will work to minimize disruptions and maintain access whenever possible. The park will be closed during the second phase, which includes improvements to landscaping and walkways and creation of a new pond and seating area.

While the project is underway, light rail customers can follow posted detours around the perimeter of the construction site to travel to and from the Orchard Station pedestrian bridge.

alerts.header: Route 0L Proposed Service Change:
alerts.description:
Change
Return service to the former peak-only level, eliminating midday service provided to reduce impacts related to the Downtown Rail Reconstruction Project.

Reason
Align service levels with the completion of the Downtown Rail Reconstruction Project and current operating needs.

alerts.header: Route 3 Proposed Service Change:
alerts.description:
Change
Increase weekday frequency to 30 minutes between Aurora Metro Center and Alameda Station from 6:00 a.m. to 8:00 p.m., and to 15 minutes between Federal Center Station and Alameda Station from 6:00 a.m. to 6:00 p.m.

Reason
Provide more frequent service during periods of higher customer demand and improve connections between Alameda Station and the Aurora and Federal Center areas.

alerts.header: Route 7 Proposed Service Change:
alerts.description:
Change
Extend service to a new terminal at 136th Outlet Mall in the City of Thornton.

Reason
Expand access to the 136th Outlet Mall area and provide additional connections for customers in Thornton.

alerts.header: Route 8 Proposed Service Change:
alerts.description:
Change
Extend service span to 9:00 p.m. on weekdays and Saturdays, and to 8:00 p.m. on Sundays, as identified in the System Optimization Plan (SOP).

Reason
Implement the System Optimization Plan recommendation to provide service later in the evening and better align the route's service span with customer needs.

alerts.header: Route 12 Proposed Service Change:
alerts.description:
Change
Add a new service pattern between 38th•Blake and Alameda Station, operating every 30 minutes on weekdays.

Reason
Provide a new connection between 38th•Blake and Alameda Station and expand travel options along the corridor.

alerts.header: Route 14 Proposed Service Change:
alerts.description:

Extend the evening service span on weekdays and Saturdays.

Reason

alerts.header: Route 19 Proposed Service Change:

alerts.header: Route 24 Proposed Service Change:

alerts.header: Route 28 Proposed Service Change:

alerts.header: Route 43 Proposed Service Change:
alerts.description:

Return weekday peak frequency to 15 minutes from the 7.5-minute service provided to reduce impacts related to the Downtown Rail Reconstruction Project.

Reason
Align service levels with the status of the Downtown Rail Reconstruction Project and current customer demand.

alerts.header: Route 49 Proposed Service Change:
alerts.description:
Change
If approved, Route ART would be discontinued and its service area would be served by Route 49. The new Route 49 would provide additional connections and operate from 5:00 a.m. to 9:00 p.m. at 30-minute frequency, with 60-minute frequency from 9 p.m. to midnight on weekdays and Saturdays.
